newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya coffee sector calls for new marketing drive.
newsitem.headline: Kenya coffee sector calls for new marketing drive.

text.p: Kenya's coffee industry has set the expansion of markets across Africa, Asia and the Middle East as its principal objective.
A technical working group under the agriculture ministry called for an intensified sales initiative in existing markets and in a 23-member grouping of eastern and southern Africa countries.
The group's report, passed to Reuters on Tuesday, also called for the extension of markets to the Middle East and the emerging economies of Eastern Europe and consolidation in the Americas.
The technical working group was appointed in May to liaise with the government on implementing the recommendations of a task force appointed by the agriculture minister.
President Daniel arap Moi said on Friday his government had adopted the group's report.
The report called for increased output through increased plantings in new areas and more diversification into new high-yielding and high-qualify varieties of coffee.

It called for the enhancement of yields among smallholders whose current average yield is about half that of the estates, and a restructuring of industry bodies to achieve greater managerial responsibility.
"This will prepare principal stakeholders, particularly farmers, and institutions for greater operational efficiency in the emerging liberalised economic environment," it said.

The report called for reduced deductions by cooperatives and enhanced tertiary processing to increase the added value of Kenya coffee. It said such moves would stabilise prices and increase returns to farmers.
It called for a system of prompt payment to farmers for delivered coffee.

The report advised the modernisation of auctions to strengthen participation by the various stakeholders. It urged the introduction of an "open market, demand-driven system, spot, options (and) futures market" in the framework of a commodities exchange.
"All this, without private treaty," it said.
Moi said the weekly export auction would remain the only method of selling Kenyan coffee and has given more autonomy to the Coffee Board of Kenya as the main marketing agency.
Several industry players, including main millers Kenya Planters' Cooperative Union and Thika Coffee Mills, have in recent weeks asked the government to allow other agencies to market coffee.
Moi said that would distort marketing.
